side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "A proposal seats at most once. A widening that cites an acceptance an admitted widening has already consumed is not admissible, so one invitation never admits twice."
side_b: CC 3.2 "The founder's standing **`membership:proposal:v1`** is then addressed to any requester — its `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance rather than fixed at proposal"
note: A builder of 'a proposal seats at most once' spends the standing proposal on the first joiner, so an open room admits one person per proposal; a builder of CC 3.2 admits every requester. Admission rule (5) ('P has not already seated K'), CC 3.2 and the CC 8.10 guard (spent per acceptance) support the per-joiner reading; the 'seats at most once' sentence needs the standing offer excepted.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "`expires_at` is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its `asserted_at` and at most 30 days later."
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 "the founder's **standing** proposal to any requester, whose `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance"
note: Nothing says whether a standing proposal carries the 30-day expiry. Read literally an open room closes every 30 days until the founder re-issues; read as 'standing' it never lapses. family_model.json subject_rule applies 'expires_at <= 30 d' to both.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "an acceptance or decline is the invitee's only — the signer resolves (`signer_acts_for`, [CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md)) to the proposal's `subject_key_ids[0]`"
side_b: CC 3.1.3.2 "the founder's **standing** proposal to any requester, whose `subject_key_ids` is resolved at acceptance"
note: The emitter rule of the same registry row has no arm for a standing proposal, whose subject list is empty: a door built from the Reserved cell refuses every acceptance of one. The description cell and CC 3.2 give the exception.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.8 "the JSON object of [CC 2.6.1.7](#2.6.1.7) stays the signed object of every earlier candidate"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:share:{class} body {"member": "salt", "type": "bstr .size 16", "presence": "required", "in_cddl": true, "cc_ref": "CC 2.6.1.8"}
note: The family model (and the CC 8.10 cards: 'Body: `for_key_id`, `period`, `return_token`, `share_index`, `salt`') marks `salt` required on census:share, census:member:share, ballot:moderator and ballot:tally. `salt` is a member of the planned v62 object only (manifests/signed_object_v2.cddl); the CC 2.6.1.7 table and signed_object.cddl of this edition have none. A door built from the body cell refuses every census return of the current edition. The text is consistent; the data mixes editions (and puts the salt on ballot:tally, a composite, which CC 2.6.1.8 does not name).

side_a: CC 4.5.13 "a first-run or consent item runs the self row, one voice of one, no window"
side_b: data manifests/choice_item.cddl "(self_choice for a first-run or consent item)"
note: The text calls it 'a row of the governance policy table above' and the CDDL names it `self_choice`; constitution/governance_policy.tsv has no such row. Its only self rows are self_roster_add and self_roster_evict (two_path, 86 400 s window), and transitions.json calls the one-voice policy `selfAct`. Three names, and the table lacks the row the text says an item runs.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 "the ballot and the acceptance are the rows of [CC 3.1.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.4), `ballot:moderator:v1` and `ballot:moderator_acceptance:v1`"
side_b: CC 3.1.3 "**A member's ballot in a moderator election** ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.5.13)): `community_id`, the election id"
note: Citation: the two ballot rows are registered in CC 3.1.3 (the mesh census and the secret poll table), not CC 3.1.4 (transport and delivery).

side_a: CC 1.13.3.3 "per-node composites publish the median bucket, which moves at most one bucket below a fifth of returns forged"
side_b: CC 6.1.9 "A composite is a histogram per field per cell. A reader computes the median bucket and the trimmed statistics from it, and a relief reads the median."
note: The threat table has the composite publish a median and calls it per-node; the home publishes the whole histogram with exact field sums, per class and period, and the median is the reader's. CC 6.1.9 is the home and CC 3.1.3 agrees with it.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "An explicit JSON `null` on an optional member is refused as malformed"
side_b: CC 2.1 "`membership:proposal`, nullable; restated on `membership:acceptance`"
note: 'nullable' and 'null' are used for 'may be absent': also CC 2.6.1.2 '`null` (no role offered)', CC 3.1.3.2 'the offered `role` (nullable)', CC 3.3.5 'valid_until: Option<rfc3339> // null = indefinite'. An emitter that writes `"role":null` is refused envelope_member_null. CC 2.6.1.7 says so for oversight_mode only.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on the accord's charter"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.2 "member absent (no holder can self-rotate; recovery is a roster change)"
note: For every other family-required member CC 2.6.1.2 says 'on one, admission refuses'; for recovery_commitments it describes a working charter without the member. CC 2.1 and CC 4.2.6 ('Every holder carries a recovery key, committed in the accord's charter at seating') support REQUIRED. CC 2.6.1.2 is informational; family_model.json has the presence 'unstated'.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "An **acceptance** or **decline** is the answer of that node's **owner**, naming the proposal by `references_attestation_id` and `proposal_hash`."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on membership:acceptance and membership:decline"
note: The signed-object table (data: constitution/signed_object.tsv, signed_object.cddl line 71) requires proposal_hash on the membership answers only; the lineage_witness answers that CC 3.1.3 says carry it are not listed, and family_model.json has no body for lineage_witness (gap). Same class as C356.

side_a: data manifests/choice_item.cddl "the verbs of manifests/transitions.json, no other"
side_b: CC 4.5.13 "an **impact** that is not written by hand but **derived from the family model** for those rows"
note: choice_item.cddl and transitions.json spell the verb `supersede`; the `verbs` cell of manifests/family_model.json spells it `replace` (76 families). An impact derived from the family model for a write whose verb is `supersede` finds no such verb there. One token is needed.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 "the axis identity (`at_rest_sha256` and `owner_key_id` on `content`; `community_key_id`, `minter_key_id` and `epoch` on `epoch`; `stream_id`, `epoch` and `owner_key_id` on `stream`)"
side_b: CC 3.3.2 "The key's identity is `(at_rest_sha256, cohort_scope, owner_key_id)` for `content`, `(community_key_id, minter_key_id, epoch)` for `epoch`, `(stream_id, epoch)` for `stream`."
note: Two lists of the axis identity in one section: the first has owner_key_id in a stream wrap's identity and no cohort_scope in a content wrap's; the second the reverse. The identity is the union and idempotence key ('Rows with distinct axis identities coexist'), so the two lists dedupe differently at the margin.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end (census_return_expired after it)."
side_b: CC 8.10 "Body: `for_key_id`, `period`, `return_token`, `share_index`, `salt`"
note: The family model body of census:share and census:member:share omits `expires_at`, which the signed-object table and CC 3.1.3 ('`expires_at` = the period's end') require on them.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on a witnessed lineage's charter"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json trust:{job}:{version} body members: attach_window_secs, attached_head_digest, pre_rotation_commitment, recovery_commitments
note: The trust body cell states four of the charter's members and omits witness_cadence_secs, witness_quorum, witnesses, halt_fuse_secs, recovers and successor_keys, all in the CC 2.6.1.7 table for this family; recovery_commitments and pre_rotation_commitment carry presence 'unstated' against REQUIRED and OPTIONAL.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1 "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Consumer-policy staleness, independent of expires_at."
note: Still present. CC 2.1 now says REQUIRED on session:*, but the CC 2.6.1.7 row is still OPTIONAL with no session clause (signed_object.cddl: '? valid_until: rfc3339-ms,  ; OPTIONAL; default absent') and the family_model.json session body lists session_id, claimed_at, community_id only. The CC 8.10 card does carry 'expiry required `valid_until`'.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "`expires_at` is REQUIRED on a proposal, after its `asserted_at` and at most 30 days later."
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED on census:share:{class}:v1 and census:member:share:v1, where it is the period's end"
note: Still present. The expires_at row of the signed-object table lists only the census shares; a door built from it admits a membership or lineage_witness proposal with no expiry. family_model.json membership body has the presence 'unstated'.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "Distinct owners behind the composite; below 10 the cell is refused census_composite_below_k."
side_b: CC 3.1.3 "refusals `ballot_tally_partials_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_mass_total_mismatch`, `ballot_tally_duplicate_period`, `aggregation_meta_dominated`"
note: Still present. The source_count note sits on a member required on census:composite and ballot:tally alike, so it refuses a room's poll of fewer than ten voters; CC 3.1.3 and CC 6.1.9 give a tally the dominance gate only.

side_a: CC 6.1.9 "`max_source_multiplicity` is `1` on every census composite by construction"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "The largest multiplicity cluster; aggregation_meta_multiplicity above the floor."
note: Half fixed: CC 3.1.3 now says 'A `max_source_multiplicity` other than `1` is refused as well'. The CC 2.6.1.7 gloss still gives only the general floor, and no refusal token is named for the census case.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 "The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`."
side_b: CC 3.3.2 "Both rows above are the frozen snake_case forms."
note: Still present (held). The wrap table keeps a v1 row and says v2 is 'MANDATORY for streaming epoch-DEK grants', which reads as v1 being admissible on a content grant; the key-wrap rule and CC 3.1.3 say v2 only.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "dimension prefix on `scores`: `key_grant:{axis}:v1` ([CC 3.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)), or the `consent:scope:*` family"
side_b: CC 3.3.1 "A `consent:scope:{kind}` dimension row, if anyone emits one, is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing"
note: Still present outside the two sections C188 settled. CC 2.4.1.2.1 still names the consent:scope:* dimension as a grant's wire discriminator, and CC 4.5.13 has a viewer publish 'a `consent:scope:view` qualifier'. CC 2.1 and CC 3.3.1 put the scope in the `scope` member of consent:state:granted.

side_b: data manifests/governance_policy.json "rule": "base(N) = N if N <= k else max(min, k + (N - k) // tail); rows with base=standing use N"
